title: Choose the visual world
question: The roll assigned Silkscreen Datasheet. Keep it, take an alternate, or re-roll.

options.label: Silkscreen Datasheet
options.lineage: GPU reference design: black soldermask, white legend, copper nets, gold fingers
options.thesis: The landing page is the board the tester already owns: every fact is a silkscreen note, Download is seating the edge connector.
options.viewport: One continuous board field: huge silkscreen wordmark, a printed grant line, gold-finger Download along the bottom edge.
options.risk: Reads as generic hardware-startup chrome if traces decorate instead of carrying nets to facts.

raised.raise: ONE LIVE NET — a single copper net and amber LED are the only live accent; everything else stays silkscreen-quiet.
BOARD OWNS THE SHEET — the first viewport is one continuous soldermask field, not a hero card on a page.
SCALE IS THE HIERARCHY — thesis at board scale; nav and meta as 0402 reference designators.
STATE IS A PHYSICAL EVENT — grant and deny occupy fixed pads; change is a layer cross-fade, not a hover tint.

options.label: Capability Map
options.lineage: seL4 capDL / Lampson access matrix as a graphic system
options.thesis: The page is an unforgeable grant table: each Preview power is a token the tester can read, not a feature tile.
options.viewport: A full-width grant matrix: rows are powers, columns are grant/deny/revoke; Download is issuing the Preview session token.
options.risk: Also the direction most runs in this category land on: capability tables are the obvious artifact for this product.

options.label: Title Sequence
options.thesis: One idea per full-bleed card: not a chat app, then the grant, then seat the install.
options.viewport: Timed cards on a flat field; the last card is Download as a cut-paper edge seating into a slot.
options.case: Holds product clarity (one claim per card); loses audience identification (film titles are not this tester’s world).
options.risk: Reads as a movie poster if the cards stay decorative and the grant never becomes a symbol that does work.

options.label: Quoted Hazard
options.lineage: Industrial streetwear: literal quotes, zip-tie tags, 45° hazard stripe
options.thesis: The obvious is printed in quotes: “NOT A BOOTABLE OS”, “NVIDIA REQUIRED”, Download keeps its orange zip-tie on.
options.viewport: Giant quoted honesty line, a diagonal hazard under the only live action, label plates for every zone.
options.case: Holds product clarity (honesty is the graphic); loses audience identification (stockroom fashion is not the tester’s scene).
options.risk: Becomes a streetwear lookbook if the quotes decorate instead of naming the real limits.

options.label: Neon Night
options.thesis: A tower of signs the tester climbs; one scarlet mark is the live grant.
options.viewport: A tall stack of signs; the red grant holds the center of gravity.
options.case: Loses both axes: cyber-neon is the AI-wrapper rut this tester was told to refuse, and rain-night hides Preview honesty.
options.kept: One live accent at the center — donated as ONE LIVE NET.
options.risk: Looks like every other agent-product night city.

options.label: Indoor Sun
options.lineage: Monofrequency hall, mirrored ceiling, sodium amber
options.thesis: One vast amber hall; the tester walks the long axis toward the light.
options.viewport: A half-sun on the far wall completing itself in the ceiling.
options.case: Loses both: art-hall identification is foreign, and atmosphere swallows the grant and the install.
options.kept: Total field commitment — donated as BOARD OWNS THE SHEET.

options.label: Type Specimen
options.thesis: One giant letter; sliders remap the whole page.
options.viewport: A single glyph filling the screen; a monospace readout of axis values.
options.case: Loses both: foundry culture is not this audience, and sliders do not map to grant or install without becoming a toy.
options.kept: Hierarchy by scale alone — donated as SCALE IS THE HIERARCHY.
options.risk: A type demo that forgets the OS.

options.label: Nixie Counter
options.thesis: Quantities are the interface: version, disk, gates as glowing digit banks.
options.viewport: A chassis of tube banks; Preview 0.1.2 is a physical count.
options.case: Loses both: closer than fashion, but numbers are not the mechanism, and the GPU they already own is the clearer artifact.
options.kept: Value change as a physical event — donated as STATE IS A PHYSICAL EVENT.
options.risk: A gadget that counts instead of granting.

canonCard.label: The category standard
canonCard.thesis: Dark AI-OS landing: kicker, centered hero, four feature cards, dual CTA, executed at full craft.
canonCard.viewport: The arrangement a visitor expects from an agent-product site.
canonCard.risk: Indistinguishable from the competition by design — the wrapper look testers were told to refuse.
